newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Spot Products -Midcon gasoline remains firm.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Spot Products -Midcon gasoline remains firm.

text.p: Prompt Midwest conventional unleaded and Gulf Coast reformulated gasoline differentials managed to gain strength late Friday despite soaring NYMEX futures, while New York gasoline eased slightly in skimpy trade.
On the NYMEX, June gasoline futures jump 1.83 cents by the settlement, while June heating oil end up 1.99 cents.

GASOLINE: Group Three conventional unleaded eased in the morning to as low as 6.0 cents above June futures before rebounding late day to offers of 7.0 cents over -- 0.25 cent firmer than Thursday diffs.

"Phillips was looking for prompt stuff toward the end of the day but couldn't find anybody willing to sell," one trader said, noting tight supplies in the market and concerns over continued late deliveries by the Explorer Pipeline offered good support.

The pipeline company acknowledged Friday it was running seven to 10 days behind schedule on deliveries into the Midwest from the Gulf, leaving little hope that 14th cycle material will reach the Midwest by the end of the month.
The delays prompted short covering and firmer diffs during the past three days, with more spirited bidding expected next week, players said.
Chicago conventional unleaded, meanwhile, eased 0.25 cent by late day from diffs seen at midday, to offers of 2.75 cents over the June print.

DISTILLATE: Diffs on low sulfur diesel eased 0.25 cent in both Group Three and Chicago, to offers of 6.0 cents over the print and 3.75 cents over, respectively, players said, noting distillates were tight but better supplied than gasoline.
GASOLINE: Conventional unleaded M1 gasoline changed hands between about 3.55 and 3.75 cents under the June futures, bouncing inside the range created earlier this week.

Some firmness was seen in the reformulated gasoline, traders said, helped by the unexpected shutdown at Phillips' Sweeny, Texas refinery and the alkylation unit outage at Citgo's Corpus Christi refinery earlier this week.
Reformulated A1 gasoline for prompt delivery was talked between 0.15 and 0.40 cent under the June NYMEX, traders said, up about 0.25 cent on the day.
DISTILLATE: Prompt heating oil barrels changed hands toward the lower end of its range, with deals seen done at 2.40 and 2.45 cents under the June NYMEX.
Trading remained very thin throughout the day, with many players attending an industry golf outing north of New York City.
Some modest weakness in the gasoline differentials was seen with prompt conventional M2 barrels talked between 2.00 and 1.75 cent under the screen, according to players.

The restart of the Tosco Trainer, Pennsylvania, refinery last weekend has yet to make a market impact, players said. The refinery, which was idled in January 1996 ahead of its sale by BP, is expected to reach its 150,000 bpd capacity next week.
